target_customer: Startups and enterprises, including healthcare and finance, that want automated security review of code and live apps
problem: Security teams are short-staffed and drowned in false positives from scanners; OpenHack aims to find and verify real vulnerabilities like a human security engineer.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI codebase scanning, AI pentesting and supply chain security
product_category: DevSecOps, AI pentesting and vulnerability management

founders.name: Ananay Arora
founders.background_notes: YC bio cites bug bounties from Meta, Apple, Perplexity, YC and DHS and authorship of CVE-2026-36755. Education not listed.

competitors.name: XBOW
competitors.traction_then: Reported to lead the HackerOne leaderboard, per vendor comparison pages
competitors.funding_then: Reported 120M USD in March 2026 and 35M USD extension in May 2026, unverified aggregator figures

competitors.name: Hadrian OpenHack
competitors.what: Open source MIT-licensed AI vulnerability research workspace with the same name
competitors.traction_then: Released May 20 2026 by Hadrian, an Amsterdam agentic pentesting company

competitors.name: Corgea
competitors.what: Packaged AI pentest for startups with published pricing

technical_complexity.rationale: Verified exploit finding with low false positives needs agent orchestration, sandboxed testing and code context; hard for a solo founder.

defensibility.rationale: Many funded rivals and an open source tool with the same name; trust badges (SOC 2, HIPAA) help but are not a moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition reported; funded AI pentesting rivals dominate coverage in 2026.

market_need_then: AI-generated code and AI-assisted attackers raised demand for automated pentesting in 2026, shown by large rounds for rivals.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened
identity.visual_style: Security SaaS page with compliance badges and sample pentest report
identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as an always-on AI security engineer

branding.community_and_virality: Founder publishes a CVE and advisories as marketing; no external brand press found.

brand_strength.rationale: Exact .com and a clear tagline, but search results for OpenHack are dominated by Hadrian's open source tool of the same name.

outcome_analysis: OpenHack is an active solo-founder Fall 2026 company with no reported funding or exit. It sells into a crowded, well funded AI pentesting market and shares its name with a May 2026 open source tool from Hadrian, which may hurt search visibility. Too early for a verdict.
notes: Funding search found nothing for this company. Customers listed on the site (Pocket AI, HydraDB, Docura Health, Neatlogs, MarginMed, Melty) are company claims. XBOW figures come from vendor comparison pages.
